problems.title: A percentage increase in area
problems.question: A rectangle’s length is doubled and width tripled. By what percentage does its area increase?
problems.idea: Multiply the scale factors before calculating the increase.
steps: The new area is (2l)(3w)=6lw=6A.
The increase is 5A, or 500% of the original area.

problems.title: Integer points on a parabola
problems.question: How many integer-coordinate points lie on $y=x^2/3-x/2+1/2$ for $-17\le x\le34$?
problems.idea: Require the numerator over 6 to be divisible by both 2 and 3.
steps: Divisibility by 2 requires x odd. Divisibility by 3 requires x divisible by 3.
Thus x=6k+3. In the interval the possible values are −15,−9,−3,3,9,15,21,27,33.
Each gives exactly one integer y.

problems.title: Two altitudes and one common area
problems.question: A triangle has sides 3 and 4. The altitudes to these sides sum to 2.1. Find the area.
problems.idea: Express both altitudes using the same area S.
steps: Hence S=1.8. This is possible because the sine of the included angle is 2S/(3·4)=0.3.

problems.title: Substitute an absolute value into a sign chart
problems.question: Solve $f(|x|)<0$, where $f(t)=t^2(t+1)/((t-3)(t+2))$.
problems.idea: The input t=|x| is nonnegative.
steps: For t>0 the fraction is negative exactly when t−3<0, so 0<t<3.
t=0 gives zero and t=3 is undefined.
Thus 0<|x|<3.

problems.title: Count roots after setting t equal to the absolute value
problems.question: For which real a does 6|x|+a=x² have exactly two distinct real solutions?
problems.idea: Each positive root t=|x| produces two x-values; t=0 produces one.
steps: For a<−9 there are no t-roots. For a=−9 there is one positive t=3, giving two solutions.
For −9<a<0 both t-roots are positive, giving four solutions. For a=0, t=0,6 gives three.
For a>0 only 3+√(9+a) is nonnegative, giving two.

problems.title: An inradius from two sides and the included angle
problems.question: AB=3, AC=5, angle A=120°. Find the triangle’s inradius.
problems.idea: Find the third side, area and semiperimeter.
formulas: BC²=AB²+AC²−2AB·AC cos A; S=AB·AC sin A/2; r=S/s.

problems.title: A rational inequality with a forbidden point
problems.question: Solve $(x^2-x)/(x-1)>6/(x-1)$.
problems.idea: Move everything to one side and factor before checking signs.
steps: The critical numbers are −2,1,3; x=1 is excluded.
The signs on the four consecutive intervals are −,+,−,+.
Use the positive intervals, excluding zeros because the inequality is strict.

problems.title: Overlap of two rotated right triangles
problems.question: An isosceles right triangle with legs 2 is rotated 45° about its right-angle vertex. Find the shaded overlap shown.
problems.idea: Use coordinates to identify the overlap polygon.
formulas: A polygon’s area is half the absolute cross-product sum of consecutive vertices.
steps: Choose the first triangle’s vertices as O=(0,0),(0,2),(2,0). The rotated triangle has other vertices (−√2,√2),(√2,√2).
The overlap vertices in order are (0,0),(0,√2),(2−√2,√2),(1,1).
Their cross-product sum has absolute value 4√2−4. Divide by 2.

problems.title: Similar triangles formed by altitude feet
problems.question: AA₁ and BB₁ are altitudes of ABC, B₁C=6, BB₁=8, and area A₁B₁C=9. Find area ABC.
problems.idea: The small triangle at C is similar to ABC.
formulas: BC=√(6²+8²); cos C=CB₁/CB; area ratio=cos² C.
steps: BC=10, so cos C=3/5.
Because CA₁=CA cos C and CB₁=CB cos C, the two sides around angle C are scaled by 3/5.
Thus 9/S=9/25, and S=25.

problems.title: Recover a trapezoid’s bases from its angles
problems.question: A trapezoid has smaller base 2, smaller leg 4, and angles 60° and 30° at its larger base. Find its area.
problems.idea: The shorter leg makes the larger angle with the base.
steps: The height is 2√3. The horizontal projections are 2 and 6.
Therefore B=2+2+6=10.

problems.title: The second diagonal of a parallelogram
problems.question: A diagonal of length b is perpendicular to a side of length a. Find the other diagonal.
problems.idea: Find the other side using the right triangle, then use the parallelogram law.
steps: Substitute c²=a²+b².
Then d²=2a²+2(a²+b²)−b²=4a²+b².

problems.title: When the larger of two expressions is at most 2
problems.question: Find x such that max(3x+1,11−x²)≤2.
problems.idea: Both expressions must be at most 2.
steps: The first gives x≤1/3. The second gives x≤−3 or x≥3.
Intersect these sets.

problems.title: A rhombus inside an equal-diagonal quadrilateral
problems.question: M,N,K,P are consecutive side midpoints of a convex quadrilateral ABCD whose diagonals are equal. Express its area S using the midpoint figure.
problems.idea: The midpoint parallelogram is a rhombus and has half the original area.
steps: Equal original diagonals imply MN=NK, so MNKP is a rhombus.
The four corner triangles together have half of ABCD’s area, so area(MNKP)=S/2.
Thus S/2=MK·NP/2.

problems.title: Complete the square in a shifted variable
problems.question: Find the minimum of f(x)=2(x−3)²−12(x−3)+7.
problems.idea: Set t=x−3 and complete the square.
steps: The square is nonnegative.
It vanishes at t=3, equivalently x=6.

problems.title: A square root with a single allowed input
problems.question: Describe the graph of y=√(−x²−4−4x)+2.
problems.idea: The radicand is the negative of a square.
steps: A real square root requires −(x+2)²≥0. This holds only at x=−2.
At that input y=2.

problems.title: Integers outside a square-root domain
problems.question: Find the sum of integer x for which √(2x²−x−4) is undefined over the reals.
problems.idea: The radicand must be negative for an undefined real value.
steps: The endpoints are approximately −1.186 and 1.686.
The integers strictly between them are −1,0,1. Their sum is 0.

problems.title: A semicircle tangent to both legs
problems.question: In right triangle ABC, AB=m, BC=n. A semicircle has its centre on hypotenuse AC and touches both legs. Find its radius.
problems.idea: The centre is equally distant from the two perpendicular legs.
formulas: With B=(0,0), A=(m,0), C=(0,n), the centre is (r,r); AC: x/m+y/n=1.
steps: Insert (r,r) into the hypotenuse equation: r/m+r/n=1.
Multiply by mn and solve r(m+n)=mn.

problems.title: Match triangle area ratios in the diagram
problems.question: Find the total shaded area in the printed diagram with regions labelled 2,1,2,6,8.
problems.idea: Triangles with the same altitude have areas proportional to their bases.
formulas: Area ratio=base ratio when heights agree; opposite products are equal for four triangles formed by quadrilateral diagonals.
steps: In the small upper triangle, the two lower pieces have areas 1 and 2, so the horizontal base is split 1:2. The upper pieces use those same bases.
The unshaded upper piece is 2, so the shaded upper piece is 4.
In the lower quadrilateral the diagonal regions have areas 6,8,3 and t, where 3=1+2. Thus 6t=8·3, giving t=4.
The two shaded pieces total 4+4=8.

problems.title: Isolated zeros in a rational sign system
problems.question: Solve $f(x+1)\le0$, $f(x+2)\ge0$ for $f(t)=(t-2)^2/(t-1)$.
problems.idea: Keep numerator zeros as well as the denominator sign.
steps: The first condition gives x<0 or x=1, excluding x=0.
The second gives x>−1 or x=0, excluding x=−1.
Their intersection is (−1,0) together with the isolated point 1.
problems.note: The printed option (−1,0) omits x=1, where the first fraction is zero and the second is positive.

problems.title: Substitute a known x-intercept
problems.question: y=ax²+2x+a has an x-intercept at x=−√3. Find a.
problems.idea: At an x-intercept y=0.
steps: This is 4a−2√3=0.

problems.title: Use a parabola’s axis of symmetry
problems.question: The graph of F(x)=−mx²+(3−m)x+m−1 has symmetry axis x=1. Find m.
problems.idea: Use the vertex formula, requiring a genuine quadratic.
steps: Here the axis is (3−m)/(2m), with m≠0.
Set (3−m)/(2m)=1. Then 3−m=2m.

problems.title: An inequality only needs one suitable input
problems.question: For which a does $(x+2)/(x^2+a^2)<1$ have a real solution?
problems.idea: Try one input that works for every parameter.
steps: The fraction is 5/(9+a²)≤5/9<1 for every real a.
Thus every real parameter has at least one solution.

problems.title: Factor a quartic inequality
problems.question: Solve x⁴−x³−12x²<0.
problems.idea: A nonzero square does not change the sign.
steps: The two linear factors have negative product for −3<x<4.
Remove x=0 because then the full expression equals zero.

problems.title: Build a quadratic from sums of its roots
problems.question: Roots a,b satisfy a+b=2 and a²+b²=10. Find a monic quadratic equation with these roots.
problems.idea: Recover ab from the square of the sum.
steps: 10=4−2ab gives ab=−3.
Substitute the sum and product.

problems.title: Count roots of a quadratic in an absolute value
problems.question: How many real solutions satisfy (√7x+√3)²+|√7x+√3|+3√5−7=0?
steps: Since 7>3√5, the right side is positive. The function t²+t is strictly increasing from 0 on t≥0.
So there is exactly one positive t.
The equations √7x+√3=t and √7x+√3=−t have two distinct real solutions.
